# 1. Introduction 

The CIELAB colour profiles of images of three sediment cores sampled from Lake Hillier were used to estimate their relative depths. Pearson cross-correlation of the cores' L* dimensions identified a set of plausible offsets, with the strongest peaks producing visually plausible alignments despite relatively weak correlation coefficients. The repeated light and dark banding also produced a periodic pattern in the cross-correlation, giving rise to several competing peaks. Horizons that appear to correspond between cores also vary in thickness, possibly due to differences in sediment accumulation rates or differential compression during sampling.

# 2. Data and Methods

We use images and colour profile data for cores MI-24-02, MI-24-03 and MI-24-04. The cores MI-24-03 and MI-24-04 each consist of two physical sections, upper (A) and lower (B), with a separate image for each, while MI-24-02 is represented by a single image. Sedivis was used to crop the images, calibrate their depth scales and extract colour data by averaging the RGB pixel values across each row, then converting the resulting values to CIELAB colour space using a D65 reference white.

# Loading the data
load_data = function(folder, file) {
  file_path = file.path(folder, file)

  df = read_excel(
    path = file_path,
    sheet = 1
  )

  df = subset(df, select = -c(layer_title, image_row_px))

}

We first investigate the autocorrelation of L* values for each core.
The ACF figures show

```{r analysis-settings}
depth_step = 0.5
max_lag_mm = 1000


max_translation_mm = 500
max_warp_mm = 100
coarse_translation_step_mm = 10
fine_translation_step_mm = 0.5
```


We note that the depth intervals differ between cores:
```{r depth-intervals, echo=FALSE}
list(
  "MI-24-02" = range(diff(core_2$depth_mm)),
  "MI-24-03" = range(diff(core_3A$depth_mm)),
  "MI-24-04" = range(diff(core_4A$depth_mm))
)
```

We therefore resample all colour profiles to a common 0.5 mm interval before analysis.
```{r resample-depth, include=FALSE}

# Resampling all profiles to 0.5 mm depth intervals
resample = function(series, depth_step = 0.5) {

  depth = seq(
    ceiling(min(series$depth_mm) / depth_step) * depth_step,
    floor(max(series$depth_mm) / depth_step) * depth_step,
    by = depth_step
  )

  series |>
    reframe(
      depth_mm = depth,
      across(
        -depth_mm,
        ~ approx(
          series$depth_mm,
          .x,
          xout = depth,
          ties = mean
        )$y
      )
    )
}

core_2  = resample(core_2)

core_3A = resample(core_3A)
core_3B = resample(core_3B)

core_4A = resample(core_4A)
core_4B = resample(core_4B)
```



```{r pearson-cross-correlation, echo=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, fig.align='center'}

pairs = list(
  c("core_3A", "core_4A"),
  c("core_3A", "core_4B"),
  c("core_3B", "core_4A"),
  c("core_3B", "core_4B")
)

for (pair in pairs) {

  core_1 = get(pair[1])
  core_2 = get(pair[2])

  image_1 = get(sub("core_", "image_", pair[1]))
  image_2 = get(sub("core_", "image_", pair[2]))

  name_1 = sub("core_", "MI-24-0", pair[1])
  name_2 = sub("core_", "MI-24-0", pair[2])

  # Pearson cross-correlation

  result = ccf(
    core_1$L_star,
    core_2$L_star,
    lag.max = round(max_lag_mm / depth_step),
    plot = FALSE
  )

  best = which.max(result$acf)

  offset_mm = as.vector(result$lag)[best] * depth_step
  correlation = as.vector(result$acf)[best]

  cat(
    pair[1], "vs", pair[2],
    "| Pearson r =", round(correlation, 4),
    "| Lag =", round(offset_mm, 1), "mm\n"
  )

  # Cross-correlation plot

  ccf_df = data.frame(
    lag_mm = as.vector(result$lag) * depth_step,
    correlation = as.vector(result$acf)
  )

  print(
    ggplot(ccf_df, aes(x = lag_mm, y = correlation)) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
      geom_segment(
        aes(xend = lag_mm, y = 0, yend = correlation),
        colour = "grey55",
        linewidth = 0.25
      ) +
      geom_vline(
        xintercept = offset_mm,
        colour = "steelblue",
        linewidth = 0.8
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste(name_1, "vs", name_2),
        subtitle = sprintf(
          "Maximum Pearson r = %.3f  |  Lag = %.1f mm",
          correlation, offset_mm
        ),
        x = "Depth lag (mm)",
        y = "Pearson correlation (r)"
      ) +
      theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
        plot.margin = margin(10, 15, 10, 10)
      )
  )

  # Aligned core images

  depth_1 = range(core_1$depth_mm)
  depth_2 = range(core_2$depth_mm) + offset_mm

  depth_min = min(depth_1, depth_2)
  depth_max = max(depth_1, depth_2)

  dimensions_1 = magick::image_info(image_1)
  dimensions_2 = magick::image_info(image_2)

  width_1 = diff(depth_1) *
    dimensions_1$width / dimensions_1$height

  width_2 = diff(depth_2) *
    dimensions_2$width / dimensions_2$height

  gap = max(width_1, width_2) * 0.3

  x1_min = 0
  x1_max = width_1

  x2_min = width_1 + gap
  x2_max = x2_min + width_2

  # Core image plot

  print(
    ggplot() +
      annotation_raster(
        as.raster(image_1),
        xmin = x1_min,
        xmax = x1_max,
        ymin = depth_1[1],
        ymax = depth_1[2],
        interpolate = TRUE
      ) +
      annotation_raster(
        as.raster(image_2),
        xmin = x2_min,
        xmax = x2_max,
        ymin = depth_2[1],
        ymax = depth_2[2],
        interpolate = TRUE
      ) +
      scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = NULL,
        limits = c(x1_min, x2_max),
        expand = expansion(mult = 0.05)
      ) +
      scale_y_reverse(
        limits = c(depth_min, depth_max),
        expand = expansion(mult = 0.02)
      ) +
      coord_fixed(ratio = 1) +
      labs(
        title = paste("Core alignment:", name_1, "and", name_2),
        subtitle = sprintf(
          "Offset = %.1f mm  |  Pearson r = %.3f",
          offset_mm, correlation
        ),
        x = NULL,
        y = "Depth (mm)"
      ) +
      annotate(
        "text",
        x = c(
          (x1_min + x1_max) / 2,
          (x2_min + x2_max) / 2
        ),
        y = depth_max + 0.04 * (depth_max - depth_min),
        label = c(name_1, name_2),
        size = 3
      ) +
      theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.line.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 25, 10)
      )
  )
}
```


## Notes 

Pearson produces peaks even between sections we don’t expect to correspond, probably due to repeated banding / chance alignment
Strongest peak not necessarily correct; use geological context and visible horizons to identify a plausible match, then Pearson to refine the offset. Need to be careful about confirmation bias when choosing the peak.


## Running with R^3 offset space

```{r}
# Search settings (mm)
offset_min = -500
offset_max = 500
offset_step = 5

# Candidate offsets
offset_values = seq(offset_min, offset_max, by = offset_step)

# Full 3D search space
offsets = expand.grid(
  offset_3B = offset_values,
  offset_4A = offset_values,
  offset_4B = offset_values
)

# Core depth ranges
range_3A = range(core_3A$depth_mm)
range_3B = range(core_3B$depth_mm)
range_4A = range(core_4A$depth_mm)
range_4B = range(core_4B$depth_mm)

# Enforce A–B ordering without overlap
offsets = subset(
  offsets,
  range_3B[1] + offset_3B >= range_3A[2] &
  range_4B[1] + offset_4B >= range_4A[2] + offset_4A
)

cat(
  "Feasible configurations:",
  format(nrow(offsets), big.mark = ","),
  "\n"
)
```


```{r}
calculate_correlations = function(offsets) {

  evaluate = function(offset_3B, offset_4A, offset_4B) {

    core_3 = rbind(
      data.frame(
        depth = core_3A$depth_mm,
        L_star = core_3A$L_star
      ),
      data.frame(
        depth = core_3B$depth_mm + offset_3B,
        L_star = core_3B$L_star
      )
    )

    core_4 = rbind(
      data.frame(
        depth = core_4A$depth_mm + offset_4A,
        L_star = core_4A$L_star
      ),
      data.frame(
        depth = core_4B$depth_mm + offset_4B,
        L_star = core_4B$L_star
      )
    )

    aligned = merge(
      core_3,
      core_4,
      by = "depth",
      suffixes = c("_3", "_4")
    )

    aligned = aligned[complete.cases(aligned), ]

    if (nrow(aligned) < 3) {
      return(NA_real_)
    }

    cor(
      aligned$L_star_3,
      aligned$L_star_4,
      method = "pearson"
    )
  }

  offsets$pearson_r = mapply(
    evaluate,
    offsets$offset_3B,
    offsets$offset_4A,
    offsets$offset_4B
  )

  offsets
}

results = calculate_correlations(offsets)

best = results[which.max(results$pearson_r), ]

print(best)

```
